validity.recommendation: Keep the Haradh->Hawiyah gas trunkline corridor (it is real), but treat this discrete 43 km / 30 in line as GEM-internal and unverified; replace the invalid OPEC-ASB support and reconcile granularity with P1918/P1919 (see duplicate finding). Do NOT green the specs.
validity.researcher_notes: The row's ONLY gem.wiki citation is OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 p.75 (wiki_citations.json) -- a country-level statistics yearbook that does not name individual pipelines and cannot support the existence of a specifically-named 43 km / 30 in 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah' line. So the sheet's own cited support is invalid for this row. Independent evidence DOES confirm the CORRIDOR/network: Saudi Aramco's 'Haradh & Hawiyah' non-associated (Khuff/Jauf/Unayzah) gas increment, and Saipem's South Gas Compression Plant Pipelines project (completed Jan 2024) which built >700 km of flowlines, trunklines and transmission lines carrying gas from the Haradh area to the Hawiyah Gas Plant (World Pipelines, Pipeline Technology Journal, SaudiGulf Projects -- all tracing to the Saipem completion PR, so effectively one origin). BUT no independent source, and neither of the two independent trackers, names a discrete 43 km / 30 in Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah line: GulfPub PE World Map's 20-feature Saudi gas roster does not list it at all, and GlobalData (offshore-technology.com) models the whole Haradh-Hawiyah system as ONE 450 km / 36 in line (which corresponds to GEM's P3961 Madrakah-Al Hawiyah, not this row). Conclusion: the corridor is real and Aramco-operated, but this specific line as specified (name + 43 km + 30 in) is unverified outside GEM. Geometry note: Haradh field (~24.14N, 49.07E) to Hawiyah Gas Plant (~24.80N, 49.39E) is ~80 km straight-line, roughly double the stated 43 km, so 'Haradh Khuff' is a mid-corridor Khuff gathering origin, not Haradh town/plant -- the stated 43 km is internally plausible only as a partial segment.

validity.recommendation: Human de-dup / segmentation review of the P1917 / P1918 / P1919 triple. Confirm whether three physically distinct parallel Haradh-Hawiyah trunklines truly exist (Aramco networks do run parallel lines) or whether this is a triple-count of one line; if kept, differentiate them (distinct endpoints/KP ranges/diameters).
validity.researcher_notes: P1917 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah', P1918 '...2', P1919 '...3' are three byte-identical rows: all len=43.00 km, dia=30 in, status=operating, updated 2022-07-19, same vague endpoints ('Saudi Arabia' -> 'Al Hawiyah'). No distinguishing attribute. The Saipem network genuinely includes multiple parallel trunklines, so three parallel lines are physically plausible, but three identical undifferentiated entries sourced only to a stats yearbook read as likely over-segmentation / triple-count and need a human de-dup decision. Related nearby Khuff-gathering rows in the same cluster (P1914 Waqr Khuff-Haradh 50km/30in, P1920 Tinat Kuff-Haradh 43km/20in) share the same 2022-07-19 bulk-import signature and warrant the same skepticism.

validity.recommendation: Change EndState/Province from 'Makkah' to 'Eastern Province' (Ash Sharqiyah). The Hawiyah Gas Plant in Ghawar is in Eastern Province; 'Makkah' is the wrong Hawiyah (a Taif-area place name).
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet has EndLocation='Al Hawiyah', EndState/Province='Makkah'. That is a mis-attribution: the Hawiyah Gas Plant that processes southern-Ghawar Khuff gas sits at ~24.80N, 49.39E in the Eastern Province, ~100 km southwest of Dhahran (Saudipedia; Ghawar production areas 'Ain Dar, Shedgum, Uthmaniyah, Hawiyah, Haradh are all Eastern Province). Makkah region is on the west coast and is a different 'Hawiyah'. GEM appears to have carried the Makkah tag across several Hawiyah-named rows (e.g. P1915, and P3961 Madrakah-Al Hawiyah where Makkah is correct for the Madrakah end) -- for a Haradh Khuff feed it is wrong. Owner Saudi Aramco 100% is CORRECT (Aramco owns/operates all Ghawar gas gathering & the Hawiyah plant). Classification note: this is a raw non-associated (Khuff) gas line from field to gas plant -- Aramco's own scope terms it a trunkline/transmission line, so keeping it in GGIT is defensible, but it is feed gas, not sales-gas transmission; treat as a caveat, not a reclass.

fills.researcher_notes: 'operating' supported at the network level: Saipem completed the Haradh & Hawiyah gas trunkline/transmission network in Jan 2024 and the Haradh/Hawiyah gas compression plants came online March 2023. Sources trace to the Saipem completion PR (single origin) -> medium. They confirm the corridor is operating, not the discrete 43 km line's own commissioning.
Fuel=Gas is solid: the Haradh & Hawiyah increment moves non-associated (Khuff/Jauf/Unayzah) natural gas to the Hawiyah Gas Plant; confirmed across Aramco, Saipem and trade coverage.

Saudi Aramco is the owner/operator (client of the Saipem EPC; all Ghawar gas gathering and the Hawiyah plant are Aramco). GulfPub independently lists Saudi gas lines as op=Aramco. Sources trace to the Saipem PR -> medium; owner attribution itself is not seriously in doubt.

43 km is NOT independently verifiable. No source gives a per-line length for a discrete Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah line; GlobalData models the aggregate Haradh-Hawiyah system as 450 km, and Haradh-town-to-Hawiyah-plant straight-line is ~80 km -- so 43 km can only be a mid-corridor segment. Left UNRESOLVED; no fabricated ref.

30 in is NOT independently verifiable. Saipem's scope was a mixed-diameter network (flow/trunk/transmission lines of various sizes); GlobalData cites a max 36 in for the aggregate Haradh-Hawiyah line. No source confirms 30 in for this specific segment. Left UNRESOLVED; no fabricated ref.

routes.start_name: Haradh Khuff gas gathering area, southern Ghawar (near Haradh field/Haradh Gas Plant)
routes.end_name: Hawiyah Gas Plant, Ghawar, Eastern Province
routes.corridor_desc: Runs north along the eastern flank of the Ghawar anticline within the Eastern Province, from the Khuff non-associated-gas gathering area in the Haradh/southern-Ghawar sector up to the Hawiyah Gas Plant (the Ghawar production areas run north-south: 'Ain Dar, Shedgum, Uthmaniyah, Hawiyah, Haradh). The Haradh-field-to-Hawiyah-plant straight-line is ~80 km, about double the sheet's 43 km, so the true origin ('Haradh Khuff') is a mid-corridor Khuff gathering point north of Haradh town rather than the town/plant itself. Bound is loose: the endpoints are named facilities/fields but the specific gathering-point origin and the routed alignment are not independently published.
routes.researcher_notes: End coord: Hawiyah Gas Plant centroid ~24.80N, 49.39E (public map placements + Saudipedia siting it in Ghawar/Eastern Province). Start coord: Haradh field/plant centroid ~24.14N, 49.07E (Wikipedia/gazetteer). Both are real named-place centroids, NOT invented; but they bound the FULL Haradh->Hawiyah corridor, which is ~80 km, whereas this row is 43 km, so the true start of this 43 km segment lies somewhere along the corridor north of Haradh -- I could not source that precise point, so suggested accuracy is only 'low'. No coordinates fabricated. Note the sheet's EndState/Province='Makkah' is wrong (should be Eastern Province).

summary: P1917 CONCERN (existence + duplicate + attribution): Haradh->Hawiyah gas trunkline corridor is real & Aramco-operated, but the sheet's only source (OPEC ASB 2012 stats yearbook) can't name a pipeline, no independent source/tracker (GulfPub, GlobalData) lists a discrete 43km/30in line, P1917/P1918/P1919 are identical triplets (likely over-segmentation), and EndState='Makkah' is wrong (Eastern Province).
